items.name: Pack: Windows workstation baseline
items.summary: The everyday health checks for a Windows desktop or laptop: disk space, a pending reboot, Defender, firewall, time, the event log and the agent update channel.
items.why: These are the problems that turn into tickets on a workstation. Limits are loose enough that a normal machine stays quiet.

why_settings.feature.checks: Checks are delivered to the device.
why_settings.agent.ring: Stable agent channel: workstations get agent updates after the pilot devices proved them.
why_settings.check.starter.disk_free: Warn under 20 % or 10 GB free, fail under 10 % or 3 GB: a full system drive breaks updates and profiles. Every 5 minutes.
why_settings.check.starter.pending_reboot: A reboot waiting after updates leaves the machine unpatched. Hourly, it is slow-moving.
why_settings.check.starter.av: Defender real-time protection on and signatures at most 7 days old.
why_settings.check.starter.svc_firewall: The Windows Firewall service (mpssvc) must run; without it the firewall is off.
why_settings.check.starter.svc_time: Windows Time must run or Kerberos and certificates start failing.
why_settings.check.starter.svc_eventlog: Without the Event Log service nothing is audited and many components fail.
why_settings.check.starter.time_skew: Clock offset from pool.ntp.org: warn over 1 s, fail over 5 s (Kerberos allows 5 minutes, so this is an early warning). Hourly.

items.note_windows_update: Windows Update is not a service check: wuauserv is trigger-started and would flap. Updates are covered by the patch policies.

items.name: Pack: Windows server baseline
items.summary: The workstation checks with stricter disk limits, the core server services, certificate expiry and disk health. Add the role add-ons for DNS, DHCP, AD DS and the rest.
items.why: A server has more to lose than a workstation: thresholds fire earlier and the server, scheduler and certificate checks are added.

why_settings.feature.checks: Checks are delivered to the device.
why_settings.check.starter.disk_free: Warn under 15 % or 20 GB free, fail under 8 % or 5 GB: the absolute limits matter on large volumes where 15 % is hundreds of GB.
why_settings.check.starter.pending_reboot: A server waiting for a reboot is unpatched; hourly.
why_settings.check.starter.av: Defender on with signatures at most 3 days old: servers are a bigger target.
why_settings.check.starter.svc_time: Windows Time must run; on a domain controller or member it keeps Kerberos working.
why_settings.check.starter.svc_server: The Server service (LanmanServer) provides file shares; stopped means shares are gone.
why_settings.check.starter.svc_scheduler: Task Scheduler runs backups and maintenance jobs.
why_settings.check.starter.svc_wmi: WMI is how most monitoring and management tools read the machine.
why_settings.check.starter.svc_dns_client: DNS Client service must run for name resolution.
why_settings.check.starter.time_skew: Warn over 0.5 s, fail over 3 s, every 30 minutes: tighter than a workstation. On a domain, set the time server to a domain controller by editing the policy.
why_settings.check.starter.cert_expiry: Machine certificates (LocalMachine\My) warn 30 days and fail 7 days before expiry, every 6 hours.
why_settings.check.starter.smart: Physical disk health (SMART) every 6 hours: the earliest sign of a failing disk.

items.name: Pack add-on: DNS server role
items.summary: Alerts when the DNS Server service stops on a server that has this role. An add-on: assign it only to servers that run the role.
items.why: A stopped DNS Server service is an outage for everything that depends on it, and nothing else in the baseline watches it.

why_settings.feature.checks: Checks are delivered to the device.
why_settings.check.role.role-dns: Service DNS must be running; checked every 2 minutes because a role outage is user visible.

items.name: Pack: Linux server baseline
items.summary: Disk and inode space, failed systemd units, the ssh, cron, log and time services, fail2ban and a pending reboot.
items.why: The usual ways a Linux server quietly breaks: a full disk or inode table, a dead cron or ssh, a clock drift, a logger that stopped.

ssh_unit.label: ssh service name (sshd on RHEL family)

cron_unit.label: cron service name (crond on RHEL family)

time_unit.label: time sync service name (chronyd on RHEL family)

why_settings.feature.checks: Checks are delivered to the device.
why_settings.check.starter.disk_free: Warn under 15 % or 10 GB free, fail under 8 % or 3 GB.
why_settings.check.starter.inodes: Inodes on / at 85 % warn, 95 % fail: millions of small files fill the inode table while df still shows free space.
why_settings.check.starter.systemd_failed: Any failed systemd unit is reported; a failed unit is a service that is not running.
why_settings.check.starter.pending_reboot: Kernel or library updates waiting for a reboot.
why_settings.check.starter.svc_ssh: ssh must run or the server cannot be managed. Service name is an install parameter.
why_settings.check.starter.svc_cron: cron runs scheduled jobs and backups. Service name is an install parameter.
why_settings.check.starter.svc_time: Time sync service. Service name is an install parameter.
why_settings.check.starter.svc_syslog: rsyslog collects logs. Service name is an install parameter. Remove the check on journald-only systems.
why_settings.check.starter.svc_fail2ban: fail2ban blocks brute force on ssh. Delete the check from your copy where it is not installed.
why_settings.check.starter.time_skew: Clock offset from pool.ntp.org, warn over 0.5 s, fail over 3 s.
why_settings.check.starter.smart: Physical disk SMART health every 6 hours; reports not applicable on virtual disks.

items.name: Pack: Laptop add-on
items.summary: Adds battery health and a "restart it, it has been on for weeks" check for Windows laptops. An add-on to the workstation baseline.
items.why: Laptops get sleep-and-resume instead of restarts, so updates stay pending, and batteries wear out silently.

why_settings.feature.checks: Checks are delivered to the device.
why_settings.feature.script_checks: Script checks run only where this is on (and the instance allows them); the two scripts are short and read only.
why_settings.check.laptop.battery: Full-charge capacity versus design capacity: warn under 70 %, fail under 50 %. Desktops without a battery report not applicable.
why_settings.check.laptop.uptime: Warn after 14 days, fail after 30 days without a restart.

items.name: Pack: Minimal / low noise
items.summary: Only the two things nobody argues about: a nearly full disk and (on Windows) real-time protection switched off.
items.why: For clients or machines where you want almost no alerts. Nothing warns early; it only fires when something is really wrong.

why_settings.feature.checks: Checks are delivered to the device.
why_settings.check.minimal.disk_free: Warn under 8 % or 2 GB, fail under 4 % or 1 GB, every 15 minutes. Applies to Windows and Linux.
why_settings.check.minimal.av: Defender real-time protection must be on; signatures may be a month old. Windows only.

items.name: Pack alerting: Workstation thresholds
items.summary: CPU and memory alerts for desktops and laptops: warn at 90 %, critical at 98 % / 97 %, only after the level has held for 15 minutes.
items.why: Workstations spike all the time; a user opening a large file is not an incident. Only sustained pressure should open an alert. Alerts that would open during a maintenance window are held back by the window itself (mute mode), and the duration requirement means a reboot or a patch run never raises one.

why_settings.feature.checks: Checks are delivered to the device.
why_settings.check.alert.cpu: Warn over 90 %, critical over 98 %, must hold 3 samples and 15 minutes, hysteresis 5 points; flapping above 60 % state changes in 20 samples holds the alert state. The agent instant verdict is set to 100 % so spikes never alert.
why_settings.check.alert.memory: Warn over 90 %, critical over 97 %, 3 samples and 15 minutes, hysteresis 3 points, same flap guard.

items.name: Pack alerting: Server thresholds
items.summary: CPU, memory and swap alerts for servers: earlier warnings (85 %), a shorter 10 minute hold, and memory pressure and swap on Linux.
items.why: A server should not sit above 85 % for long. Servers get warned sooner than workstations but still need a hold time so backups and patch runs do not page anyone. Alerts that would open during a maintenance window are held back by the window itself (mute mode), and the duration requirement means a reboot or a patch run never raises one.

why_settings.feature.checks: Checks are delivered to the device.
why_settings.check.alert.cpu: Warn over 85 %, critical over 95 %, held 3 samples and 10 minutes, hysteresis 5, flap guard.
why_settings.check.alert.memory: Warn over 88 %, critical over 95 %, held 3 samples and 10 minutes, hysteresis 3, flap guard.
why_settings.check.alert.swap: Linux only: swap use over 50 % warns and over 80 % is critical, held 20 minutes; heavy swapping means the memory estimate was wrong.
why_settings.check.alert.mem_pressure: Linux only: kernel memory pressure (PSI some avg10) over 20 warns and over 40 is critical for 10 minutes: tasks are stalled waiting for memory.

items.name: Pack alerting: Quiet (critical only)
items.summary: Only critical CPU and memory: over 98 % / 97 % for 30 minutes. No warnings.
items.why: For noisy clients: you hear about it only when a machine is effectively unusable. Alerts that would open during a maintenance window are held back by the window itself (mute mode), and the duration requirement means a reboot or a patch run never raises one.

why_settings.feature.checks: Checks are delivered to the device.
why_settings.check.alert.cpu: Critical only, over 98 % for 5 samples and 30 minutes.
why_settings.check.alert.memory: Critical only, over 97 % for 5 samples and 30 minutes.

items.note_metrics: Disk queue length and network error metrics have no threshold-capable check type in this RivetCore release, so the pack ships no preset for them.

items.name: Pack patch: Pilot (about 10 % of devices, next day)
items.summary: Approves updates automatically one day after they appear, for a pilot group, and installs them at night. Assign it to roughly one device in ten.
items.why: The pilot group finds a bad update before everyone else gets it. Pair it with the Standard policy for the rest.

why_settings.approval_mode: Automatic: the pilot is the test, a person does not have to approve each update.
why_settings.auto_days_critical: Critical updates approved 1 day after first seen.
why_settings.auto_days_security: Security updates approved 1 day after first seen.
why_settings.auto_days_important: Important updates approved 1 day after first seen. Optional and driver updates are never approved by this policy.
why_settings.install_enabled: The scheduler may install approved updates.
why_settings.window_mode: Install only inside the daily window below.
why_settings.window_days: Weekdays only, so a bad update is noticed during working hours.
why_settings.window_start: From 20:00 (the policy time zone is UTC unless you set one).
why_settings.reboot_policy: Reboots are reported, not performed: a restart by itself needs a person to confirm it on the policy.

items.name: Pack patch: Standard (Tuesday + 7 days)
items.summary: Approves security and important updates a week after they appear (the Tuesday after Patch Tuesday), and installs them in a Tuesday evening window.
items.why: A week of pilot soak time catches the bad updates; the Tuesday window gives a fixed, predictable rhythm for the main fleet.

why_settings.ring: Ring broad adds the 7 day delay; with no extra days that gives Tuesday + 7.
why_settings.auto_days_critical: No days on top of the ring delay.
why_settings.auto_days_security: No days on top of the ring delay.
why_settings.auto_days_important: No days on top of the ring delay. Optional and driver updates are never approved by this policy.
why_settings.install_enabled: The scheduler may install approved updates.
why_settings.window_mode: Daily-style window, set to one weekday.
why_settings.reboot_policy: Reboots are reported, not performed (see the Pilot policy).

items.name: Pack patch: Servers (monthly, manual approval)
items.summary: A person approves each update (a second person must agree); installation happens only in a Saturday night window. Reboots are left to you.
items.why: Servers must not patch themselves in the middle of the week. Approval, a second pair of eyes and a fixed window make it a planned change.

why_settings.ring: Ring last: sensitive machines two weeks behind the pilot.
why_settings.approval_mode: Manual: nothing is approved by itself.
why_settings.two_person: Approving an update by hand needs a second person.
why_settings.install_enabled: Approved updates may be installed in the window.
why_settings.window_days: Saturday only (run it monthly by approving once a month).
why_settings.reboot_policy: Reboots outside business hours are queued by you as a reboot job in the Saturday window; the policy never restarts a server by itself.

items.name: Pack patch: Critical only
items.summary: Approves only updates classified critical, the day after they appear. Everything else waits for a person.
items.why: For machines that must stay as they are except for emergency fixes.

why_settings.approval_mode: Automatic, but only for the kind below.
why_settings.auto_days_critical: Critical updates approved 1 day after first seen; all other kinds are never approved by this policy.
why_settings.reboot_policy: Never reboot, not even a report.
why_settings.max_minutes: An install may run one hour.

items.name: Pack window: Nightly 02:00-04:00
items.summary: Every night from 02:00 to 04:00 local time. Created switched off.
items.why: Backups, scans and updates run at night and make noise. This keeps alerts quiet during that time.

timezone.label: IANA time zone the window times are in, for example America/Chicago

why_settings.mode: Mute: checks keep running, new alerts are held back until the window ends, open alerts stay open.
why_settings.scope_type: Applies to every device; narrow the scope after installing if you only want some.
why_settings.local_start: Start time in the window time zone.

items.name: Pack window: Sunday patching 01:00-05:00
items.summary: Sundays from 01:00 to 05:00 local time. Created switched off.
items.why: A weekly patching slot for workstations, so reboots and service restarts do not raise alerts.

timezone.label: IANA time zone the window times are in, for example America/Chicago

why_settings.mode: Mute: checks keep running, new alerts are held back until the window ends, open alerts stay open.
why_settings.scope_type: Applies to every device; narrow the scope after installing if you only want some.
why_settings.local_start: Start time in the window time zone.

items.name: Pack window: Server patching Saturday 22:00-04:00
items.summary: Saturdays from 22:00 for six hours, local time. Created switched off.
items.why: The slot for the Servers patch policy, long enough for a reboot.

timezone.label: IANA time zone the window times are in, for example America/Chicago

why_settings.mode: Mute: checks keep running, new alerts are held back until the window ends, open alerts stay open.
why_settings.scope_type: Applies to every device; narrow the scope after installing if you only want some.
why_settings.local_start: Start time in the window time zone.

items.name: Pack change monitoring: server persistence and security presets
items.summary: Turns on the change-monitor watches for startup keys, local administrators and Defender exclusions on Windows, and Linux ssh, sudo and accounts. Optional.
items.why: These are the places an attacker, or an unplanned change, shows up first. Unlike the other items this is an instance-wide setting (change monitoring has no per-policy scope in this release), so installing needs an explicit confirmation and it also applies to workstations.

why_settings.presets: Windows: win.startup (Run keys, Winlogon, IFEO), win.local_admins (Administrators group), win.defender (exclusions and policy). Linux: lnx.ssh, lnx.sudo, lnx.accounts.
